title: Redwood Console: tracing + request logs debugging walkthrough
next_steps: Jordan to share pricing band and Dedicated vs Hosted TCO spreadsheet by 2027-08-10
Samir to run a 1-hour benchmarking session on Atlas's sample workload—propose timeslot w/ Luca
Priya to share sample prompt set and current latency distributions
action_items: Jordan Lee - Send Dedicated vs Hosted TCO spreadsheet - 2027-08-10
Samir Patel - Schedule benchmark run and provide runbook - 2027-08-09
Priya Nair - Share prompt set and production traces - 2027-08-08
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs for Atlas Health's inference workloads; discussed latency vs cost, KV cache insights, rolling back model variants and audit/logging for compliance; agreed on pilot benchmarks and next steps.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE. Samir our SE is here too. Quick intro round?
[00:08] Marta Ortiz: Marta, CTO at Atlas Health, we run patient triage flows and need very low latency SLOs.
[00:15] Priya Nair: Priya, head of ML, responsible for models and infra.
[00:19] Luca Romano: Luca, platform eng, I'll be doing the integration work.
[00:23] Jordan Lee: Great, goal for today is to show the Console tracing, error analysis, request logs, typical debugging flows, and talk pilot next steps.
[00:33] Samir Patel: We'll jump into the demo, keep it interactive. if you want to stop and ask feel free.
[00:37] Priya Nair: Quick context, we're currently using a mix of self-hosted Triton for embeddings and OpenAI for chat. Our P95 latency target is 300ms and spikes to 700ms sometimes during peak.
[00:52] Jordan Lee: Perfect, that helps. We'll focus on tracing to see where those spikes happen and how Request Logs can help isolate cause.
[00:59] Samir Patel: (screen share) Opening the Console—top nav, tracing tab, default timeframe set to last 24 hours. you can see traces aggregated by route.
[01:12] Samir Patel: There's a quick filter for model, region, and deployment type—hosted vs dedicated—very useful for your mixed stack.
[01:22] Priya Nair: How precise are the timestamps? We need to correlate with our infra metrics in Datadog.
[01:28] Samir Patel: They are millisecond alt, we also export to OTLP if you want. The trace IDs line up with Request Logs so you can cross-reference.
[01:38] Luca Romano: OTLP export is good. What's the retention on tracing? We need 90 days for audits.
[01:45] Jordan Lee: By default 30 days, enterprise plan can do 90+ with add-on—audit logs also available. We'll include that in the doc bundle.
[01:53] Marta Ortiz: Are audit logs tamper-evident? for compliance.
[01:56] Jordan Lee: Yes, we support append-only storage and KMS-backed signatures for Private deployments; we can share SOC2 artifacts.
[02:05] (ambient typing)
[02:12] Samir Patel: Back to trace view, clicking into a long tail trace, you can see per-segment timings: request queueing, model init, KV cache hit/miss, runtime kernel time.
[02:25] Priya Nair: KV cache—does Redwood share hit ratio metrics and suggestions?
[02:29] Samir Patel: Yeah we show cache hit rates and suggest prefixes to prewarm; Optimize can give batching + quantization recs by workload.
[02:38] Priya Nair: Nice, that could cut our 700ms spikes if it's KV-related.
[02:42] Jordan Lee: Also routing policies—if you want extremely low latency for critical routes, you can route to Dedicated pools in region A and fallback to hosted as failsafe.
[02:53] Luca Romano: What about fallback behavior—how do we ensure consistent outputs if fallback model is quantized? We can't degrade clinical accuracy.
[03:02] Samir Patel: Good point. You can pin model families and only allow fallback to validated variants; we also run regression evals tied to your prompt set.
[03:11] Priya Nair: Can we see the actual request payload for debugging? Not sure we can send PHI to a hosted endpoint.
[03:20] Jordan Lee: For privacy we redact PII by default in Request Logs for hosted; for Private you can keep full payloads under your VPC. We can also integrate with your KMS so logs are encrypted.
[03:36] Marta Ortiz: So for Atlas Health likely Private or Dedicated behind VPC; data residency matters.
[03:41] Jordan Lee: Understood.
[03:43] Samir Patel: Now show Request Logs. this table has columns: timestamp, trace id, route, model, tokens in/out, latency, error code. click a row to see full payload (redacted unless allowed).
[04:00] Samir Patel: Demo: here's a spike at 2027-08-03 09:14:22—open trace—queue time is high; request logs show concurrent batch size rose from 4 to 12.
[04:15] Priya Nair: Why would batch size increase like that? our traffic is spiky but we'd expect max batch 8.
[04:20] Samir Patel: We have adaptive batching; during lower throughput we prefer small batches but during sudden arrival bursts batching can spike. Optimize suggests knob changes.
[04:30] Luca Romano: Can we set hard caps so it never exceeds batch size 8?
[04:33] Samir Patel: Yes you can configure batch caps per route; we'll show the policy config later.
[04:38] (background: someone coughs)
[04:40] Samir Patel: Next: Error analysis. Filtered by 5xx. here's a common error: KV cache miss triggered a fallback that failed due to schema mismatch.
[04:54] Priya Nair: Schema mismatch—meaning tokenization differences?
[04:57] Samir Patel: In this case the downstream input had an extra control char; Request Logs shows the payload and we show instrumented sanitizer warnings.
[05:06] Jordan Lee: We also surface predictions with confidence bands when available so you can triage quality vs infra.
[05:13] Priya Nair: Can we map errors to codeowners internally? like route owners.
[05:17] Samir Patel: Yes, you can map route tags to teams and we surface alerts to PagerDuty/Slack with trace links.
[05:24] Luca Romano: Great. For the pilot, can we execute a small traceroute-style benchmark? we need to reproduce P95 spike.
[05:32] Samir Patel: We usually run a controlled synthetic replay using your prompt set and sample traffic pattern; we'll set the seed so it's reproducible.
[05:40] Jordan Lee: Next, drilling into request details: note the logs show variant id and quantization profile, which helps debug quality regressions after a rollout.
[05:53] Priya Nair: How do rollbacks work? we need fast rollback if quality drops.
[05:57] Samir Patel: Canary rollouts are supported; if evaluation metrics degrade we auto rollback and notify owners.
[06:05] Priya Nair: Do auto rollbacks rely on absolute thresholds? we prefer hold-and-alert for human review.
[06:10] Samir Patel: Policies are configurable—auto rollback or manual hold.
[06:14] Marta Ortiz: Security question—we need SSO/SAML and RBAC for non-prod vs prod separation.
[06:20] Jordan Lee: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and granular RBAC; console shows role-based views for request logs with PHI redaction.
[06:30] (typing noise)
[06:35] Priya Nair: Any known performance differences hosting on GCP vs AWS for your Dedicated pools?
[06:40] Samir Patel: Differences are small; kernel selection and instance types matter. we'll share our benchmark matrix and the Optimize recs per architecture.
[06:50] Luca Romano: We need cost guidance—what's tradeoff for dropping to 8-bit quantization vs fp16?
[06:56] Jordan Lee: Optimize provides cost-vs-latency curves; quantization often reduces cost 30-60% with small latency gains but sometimes increases infer time depending on kernel. we'll attach a sample curve.
[07:10] Priya Nair: For the pilot, timeline—if we start next week how long to get a Dedicated pool standing?
[07:17] Jordan Lee: Dedicated provisioning typically 7-14 days, Private on prem longer; we can accelerate for pilots with pre-configured images.
[07:26] Marta Ortiz: Can we get a security pack and SOC2 doc before exec signoff?
[07:30] Jordan Lee: Absolutely, I'll attach SOC2, encryption docs, and the audit log spec. Jordan to follow up.
[07:36] (pause)
[07:40] Samir Patel: Quick tour of the debugging workflow: identify spike in traces -> open request log -> look at payload and model variant -> check cached hit/miss -> if model variant changed, compare against evals -> roll back if needed.
[07:56] Priya Nair: Good. can we trigger replays from the Console to rerun specific traces against a new model?
[08:02] Samir Patel: Yes, there's a replay button to run a trace through a staging model or different quantization profile; outputs are stored in ephemeral sandbox.
[08:12] Luca Romano: Sandbox runs—do they consume rate limits or are they separate?
[08:16] Samir Patel: Sandbox is metered but separate from production quotas, and you can set limits.
[08:22] Jordan Lee: Let's capture next steps.
[08:25] Marta Ortiz: Quick question—does request logging add latency?
[08:28] Samir Patel: Negligible—we stream logs asynchronously; there's an opt-in for fully synchronous logging if you need absolute capture but it's rare.
[08:36] Priya Nair: Thanks all, this was useful.
[08:40] Jordan Lee: Recap: we'll send pricing and SOC2 docs, Samir will schedule benchmark; Priya will share prompt set. Agreed?
[08:47] Priya Nair: Agreed.
[08:49] Marta Ortiz: Agreed.
[08:50] Jordan Lee: Great, we'll follow up via email with docs and proposed times. Thanks everyone.
[08:55] (meeting ends)
